ground_truth.description: Staking.allocateETH() forwards ETH to LiquidityBuffer.depositETH(), which auto-allocates to defaultManagerId when shouldExecuteAllocation is true. If the current default manager is deactivated via LiquidityBuffer.updatePositionManager()/togglePositionManagerStatus() without first switching defaultManagerId or disabling auto-allocation, _allocateETHToManager(defaultManagerId, …) reverts with LiquidityBuffer__ManagerInactive(). This can unexpectedly block allocation flows.
ground_truth.root_cause: Staking.allocateETH() forwards ETH to LiquidityBuffer.depositETH(), which auto-allocates to defaultManagerId when shouldExecuteAllocation is true. If the current default manager is deactivated via LiquidityBuffer.updatePositionManager()/togglePositionManagerStatus() without first switching defaultManagerId or disabling auto-allocation, _allocateETHToManager(defaultManagerId, …) reverts with LiquidityBuffer__ManagerInactive(). This can unexpectedly block allocation flows.
ground_truth.attack_scenario:
1. Admin sets defaultManagerId to manager 0 with shouldExecuteAllocation = true
2. Admin calls togglePositionManagerStatus(0) to deactivate the default manager
3. User calls Staking.allocateETH() which forwards to LiquidityBuffer.depositETH()
4. depositETH() calls _allocateETHToManager(defaultManagerId, msg.value)
5. _allocateETHToManager reverts with LiquidityBuffer__ManagerInactive() because the default manager is inactive
6. All allocation flows are blocked until admin either reactivates the manager or changes defaultManagerId
ground_truth.fix_description: Prevent deactivation of the current defaultManagerId while auto-allocation is enabled: require shouldExecuteAllocation == false or switch defaultManagerId to an active manager before deactivation.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The contract allows deactivation of the default manager while auto-allocation is still enabled, causing depositETH() to revert. When shouldExecuteAllocation is true, depositETH() automatically allocates to defaultManagerId, but if that manager is deactivated, _allocateETHToManager() will revert with LiquidityBuffer__ManagerInactive().
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Admin sets shouldExecuteAllocation = true and defaultManagerId = X 2. Admin calls togglePositionManagerStatus(X) to deactivate manager X 3. Any subsequent call to depositETH() will fail because it tries to allocate to the now-inactive defaultManagerId 4. The entire allocation flow becomes blocked until shouldExecuteAllocation is disabled or defaultManagerId is changed to an active manager
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Prevent deactivation of the current defaultManagerId while auto-allocation is enabled by adding a check in togglePositionManagerStatus: if (managerId == defaultManagerId && shouldExecuteAllocation) revert CannotDeactivateDefaultManager();

vulnerabilities.explanation: Similar to togglePositionManagerStatus, updatePositionManager allows deactivating the default manager without checking if auto-allocation is enabled, which will cause depositETH() to revert when trying to allocate to the inactive manager.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Admin sets shouldExecuteAllocation = true and defaultManagerId = X 2. Admin calls updatePositionManager(X, newCap, false) to deactivate manager X 3. Subsequent depositETH() calls will fail with LiquidityBuffer__ManagerInactive 4. Allocation flow becomes blocked until configuration is fixed
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Add validation in updatePositionManager: if (isActive == false && managerId == defaultManagerId && shouldExecuteAllocation) revert CannotDeactivateDefaultManagerWhileAutoAllocationEnabled();

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract has a logic vulnerability where the default position manager can be deactivated while auto-allocation is still enabled, causing depositETH() to revert and blocking the allocation flow. Two functions (togglePositionManagerStatus and updatePositionManager) allow deactivation of the default manager without checking the auto-allocation status first.
